definitions.explanation: The month after this one; the coming month. Used to refer to future events or plans in the month that follows the current one.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}{何|なに}をしますか。
examples.english: What will you do next month?

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}から{仕事|しごと}を{始|はじ}めます。
{来月|らいげつ}{日本|にほん}に{行|い}きます。とても{嬉|うれ}しいです。
examples.english: I'm going to Japan next month. I'm very happy about it.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}{友達|ともだち}に{会|あ}います。{今|いま}から{待|ま}っています。
examples.english: I'll see my friend next month. I'm already waiting for it.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}は{忙|いそが}しいです。{毎日|まいにち}{勉強|べんきょう}しなければなりません。
examples.english: I'll be busy next month. I have to study every day.

notes: Part of a time reference series: {先月|せんげつ} (last month), {今月|こんげつ} (this month), {来月|らいげつ} (next month). The {来|らい} prefix means 'coming' or 'next' and also appears in {来週|らいしゅう} (next week) and {来年|らいねん} (next year).
